about: Every setting LG's Settings app (com.palm.app.settings 4.0.1, webOS 4.5) offers, as LG's category > page > item tree, with the API behind each item. Labels are our own words. Written from the app bundle and the TV's settings description offline; see SETTINGS-PLAN.md.

fields.id: settingsservice key, or our name for a non-key item
fields.meaning: what the item does, in our words
fields.api: settingsservice: {service, read, write, category, keys}; other services: {service, read/write/... method names, params}; navigation rows: {none}
fields.type: switch | enum | range | dynamic (values only at runtime) | file | info | action | form | page | device-list | network-list | list | multi-enum
fields.domain: static seed from the TV's /etc/palm/description.json (US variant where one exists); the live getSystemSettingDesc wins
fields.dimension: the settingsservice dimensions a value is stored under (input, pictureMode, _3dStatus, dynamicRange...)
fields.visibleWhen: rules LG codes on top of the description's ui.visible/ui.active
fields.confirm: what must be confirmed before writing, if anything
fields.region: page or item only exists for a country group or model
fields.unknown: what could not be determined offline

reading.settingsservice: LG reads with luna://com.webos.settingsservice/batch {operations:[{method:getSystemSettings, params:{category, keys, dimension?}}, {method:getSystemSettingDesc, params:{category, keys}}]} and keeps getSystemSettings {category, keys, subscribe:true} open. Writes are setSystemSettings {category, settings:{key:value}, dimension?}; resets are resetSystemSettings {category, keys, dimension?}. getSystemSettingValues {category, key} lists values for dynamic keys.
reading.visibility: LG decides most row visibility at runtime from getSystemSettingDesc: ui.visible hides a row, ui.active greys it, and each arrayExt entry has its own visible/active. A few rules are coded on top (visibleWhen).
reading.dimensions: Picture keys are stored per input x pictureMode x _3dStatus (and pictureMode per dynamicRange). Reading without a dimension returns the current input's values. Subscriptions fire when the input or HDR state changes.
reading.otherServices: Sleep timer: com.webos.service.tv.time getSleepTimeInfo {subscribe:true} / setSleepTimeInfo {sleepTimeMinute}. Network: com.webos.service.connectionmanager getstatus {subscribe:true}; com.webos.service.wifi findnetworks/connect/setstate/deleteprofile. Bluetooth audio: com.webos.service.btaudiosrc. Time: com.palm.systemservice getPreferences/setPreferences {useNetworkTime, timeZone}. Updates: com.webos.service.update.

identity.ours: The compositor's QML calls the bus as whatever appId its WebOSServices Service declares. Our layer uses com.webos.surfacemanager.systemui, which is in no permission group (commit 6d1b402).
identity.lgInProcess: LG's Quick Settings, inside the same compositor, calls settingsservice get/set/desc/values, tv.time sleep, btaudiosrc, pdm, wisa, config and applicationManager/launch as appId com.webos.app.quicksettings (QuickSettings/Globals.js). Several Service objects sharing one appId in one process is LG's own pattern.
identity.settingsserviceAllow: /etc/palm/settingsservice.allow lists 21 keys with read or read/write permissions (captionEnable, soundOutput, soundOutputDigital, avSync*, eArcSupport, truMotionMode, simplinkEnable, supportBnoModel; country, audioGuidance*, highContrast, storeMode... read only). It holds no pictureMode or soundMode. Hypothesis, unverified: it is the per-key allowlist for callers outside the settings groups, so com.webos.surfacemanager.systemui could not write tier-1 picture/sound keys today.
toVerifyOnTv: the compositor's client permissions (listed in /usr/share/luna-service2/manifests.d/starfish-luna-surface-manager.manifest.json): which groups com.webos.app.quicksettings and com.webos.surfacemanager* names hold

internalKeys.meaning: Keys LG's panels read only to decide visibility, labels or dimensions. Not user settings; our data layer reads some of them the same way.

lgTargets.meaning: launch params LG Settings accepts: {target} opens a page path (unknown targets fall back to Picture), {item} focuses an item, {pictureData, soundData} pre-seeds values (Quick Settings All Settings row), webOSRelaunch re-runs the same. Our Settings should accept the same targets so deep links keep working.

categories.meaning: How the TV sounds and where sound goes
